title: Airbyte is ignoring `JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST` in .env
body: I upgraded my Airbyte host from 8 GB to 32 GB of RAM after a sync terminated with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`. I set `JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST=4g` and `JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT=6g` in `.env` and restarted Airbyte, but the destination write-container log still reports a 1Gi request and 2Gi limit. Updating the Redshift destination's `actor_definition.resource_requirements` also did not change it. A connection-level `resource_requirements` value of `{"memory_limit":"4Gi","memory_request":"6Gi"}` does work, but the instance-level environment variables and connector-level setting do not.

symptoms_visible: A sync terminates with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`.
After setting the job main-container memory request and limit and restarting Airbyte, the destination write log still reports memoryRequest=1Gi and memoryLimit=2Gi.
The connection-level resource requirement changes the container resources, while my instance-level and connector-level values do not.
N0.label: N0 instance and connector overrides not reflected

symptoms_visible: The read and write containers continue to use their lower resource values, while check containers show the configured values.
Connection-specific requirements apply to the connection's containers.
N1.label: N1 job-type scope corroborated

symptoms_visible: Read and write jobs still show the lower resource values unless I use a connection-specific requirement.
N2.label: N2 platform regression recognized

symptoms_visible: With the latest containers, check and normalization pods show the configured resources, but source-read and destination-write pods still show 500m/1.5 CPU and 1Gi/1.5Gi memory values.
I am not sure whether the deployment charts also needed to be updated.
N3.label: N3 post-update deployment shows mixed values

symptoms_visible: The worker pod environment contains JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT=2, JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_REQUEST=1, JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT=5G, and JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST=1G.
Some source and destination logs still show older resource values.
N4.label: N4 environment placement inspected

symptoms_visible: A sync log now shows the configured limits for the check, source, and destination pods; I saw the override work and am satisfied the issue can be closed.
N_terminal.label: terminal resource overrides observed working

question_patterns: Which job types keep the old resource values: check, read, write, or normalization?
Do the configured values appear on check containers even though they do not appear on sync read/write containers?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The read and write containers are the ones that keep the lower values. Check containers show the configured values, and setting the requirement at the connection level works for that connection.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: None of the job types use the configured values, including check jobs and connection-specific jobs.
Read and write jobs show the same mismatch, but only the destination has reached an out-of-memory error so far.

question_patterns: Is this specific to Docker Compose, or can you reproduce it on Kubernetes as well?
Which Airbyte deployment type shows this behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I observed the exact read/write-versus-check behavior on Docker Compose. The same instance-level failure has also been reproduced on Kubernetes, where connection-specific requirements still work.

edges.comment: Opening reporter c1/c2/c5 confirms the Docker Compose behavior. Comments c0/c3/c4 contribute corroborating Kubernetes observations from other affected operators; those affected users are folded into the simulated user side without treating Kubernetes-specific setup as the opening reporter's original deployment.

solution.intent: Recognize this as the acknowledged regression in instance-wide resource requirements rather than a RAM-sizing or syntax problem, and use the working connection-specific requirement only as an interim workaround while taking the platform fix.
solution.concrete_example: The platform maintainer confirmed a regression affecting instance-wide resource requirements. Keep the connection-level requirement as a temporary workaround for urgent syncs, then update when the release restoring the previous resource-resolution behavior is available.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the differing effective resource values and the working connection-level override. The conclusion that this was a platform regression in instance-wide resource resolution came from the maintainer's diagnosis in c6.

edges.comment: Maintainer c6 explicitly accepts this as a regression in instance-wide resource requirements and confirms that connection-level requirements remain functional. This is the technical diagnosis for the opening issue.

question_patterns: Please upgrade to the current Airbyte release and rerun a sync; what resource values do the resulting pods report?
After updating your deployment, do check, read, and write jobs all report the configured limits?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am using the latest containers, although I am not sure whether I also need updated charts. Check and normalization pods show my 1G request and 5G limit, but the source-read and destination-write pods still show 1Gi/1.5Gi.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After the update, check, read, write, and normalization jobs all show the configured values consistently.
The same mixed result occurs, but the stale read/write limit is 2Gi rather than 1.5Gi.

solution.intent: Upgrade to the Airbyte release that restores the prior instance-wide resource-requirement behavior, then verify the effective resources in newly created read and write jobs.
solution.concrete_example: Airbyte 0.50.34 was announced as restoring the previous behavior. Upgrade the complete deployment and inspect the new source-read and destination-write log entries rather than relying only on check pods.

edges.comment: Maintainer c10-c11 announces the corrected release and requests a retest. A different affected Kubernetes operator supplies the post-release observations in c12-c14; the edge explicitly folds that operator into the user side rather than attributing Kubernetes charts to the opening Docker Compose reporter. The update is retained, so system state changes from S1 to S2.

question_patterns: Which Airbyte pod did you inspect when checking the environment variables?
Where are you seeing the configured JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER values in the running deployment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked the worker pod. It has JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT=2, JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_REQUEST=1, JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT=5G, and JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST=1G.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I checked the server pod and it has the intended values, but every newly created read and write pod still uses the old limits after all services were restarted.
The values are present in the worker pod with equivalent Kubernetes units such as 5Gi instead of 5G.

question_patterns: Can you paste the JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER values shown in that pod?
What exact CPU and memory request and limit values are present there?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The worker pod shows CPU request 1, CPU limit 2, memory request 1G, and memory limit 5G.

edges.comment: Affected Kubernetes operator c16 identifies the worker pod as the place inspected and pastes its raw environment. Maintainer c19 later interprets the significance of that location; that conclusion is deliberately not placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: After refreshing the deployment, rerun a sync and report the resource values shown for the newly created check, source, and destination pods.
Please retest with newly created job pods and tell me whether all of them now receive the intended limits.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I confirmed in a new sync log that the proper limits were shown for the check, source, and destination pods. Looking back, some earlier pods had new values and others had old ones, so something had not picked up my ConfigMap update. I saw it work once and I am good with closing the issue.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every newly created source and destination pod still uses the old values even after the full deployment was refreshed.
The intended values appear consistently in source and destination jobs, but I did not run a normalization job during this verification.

solution.intent: Ensure the job resource variables are available to the Airbyte server, refresh or restart the services that consume the deployment configuration, and verify the effective limits on newly created read and write pods before declaring the regression resolved.
solution.concrete_example: The JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER variables are read by airbyte-server, not merely from the worker environment. Ensure the server receives the intended ConfigMap values, roll or restart the affected Airbyte services so they pick up the configuration, then start a new sync and inspect both source-read and destination-write resource lines.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer states in c19 that JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER variables are read from airbyte-server. The explanation that mixed old and new pod values came from a service not picking up the ConfigMap is the final deployment-level inference accepted by the affected operator in c21; the user only reports the environment location and observed pod values.

edges.comment: Maintainer c19 identifies airbyte-server as the configuration consumer. In c21 the affected Kubernetes operator reports that a later sync showed the proper values for check, source, and destination pods and accepts closure, while attributing earlier mixed values to a service not picking up the update. This is folded affected-user verification, not a claim that the opening Docker Compose reporter personally performed the Kubernetes retest.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original technical cause as the acknowledged Airbyte regression in instance-wide resource requirements: global JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER settings were not being applied to sync read/write containers even though connection-specific requirements worked.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the observed split between job types and configuration levels: read/write jobs retained lower defaults, while check jobs and connection-specific requirements could show the requested values.

Must recommend using a release containing the restoration of instance-wide resource behavior and, for deployments with mixed old and new values, ensure the variables reach airbyte-server and refresh the services that consume the configuration.

Must not present the connector-level actor-definition override as the fix; it was already tried without changing the read/write resources. A connection-level override may be offered only as a temporary workaround.
Must ask the affected user to verify the effective resources on newly created source-read and destination-write jobs before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Airbyte operator who can edit `.env`, ConfigMaps, database resource-requirement JSON, inspect pod environments, and compare job logs, but needs maintainer guidance about which Airbyte service consumes each setting.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and evidence-oriented; provides exact configuration values and log excerpts, follows up when behavior differs by job type, and readily acknowledges resolution after observing a successful sync.
